sara_sales: looping in eng/support — customer hitting weird dims + rate limits on POC embedding+rerank. cc @emily_eng @kevin_ml
joe_customer: seeing 400 errors intermittently, then a flood of 429s. payload attached below. using our batching lib, 512 dims expected, but model docs say 1536. puzzled.
emily_eng: thanks — can you paste the exact request body (without PII) and the model id you requested? also which endpoint: /v1/embeddings or the rerank endpoint?
joe_customer: yep /v1/embeddings -> model: open-embed-large-v1 (we're using a wrapper that maps to redwood endpoint). sample payload:```{"inputs": ["doc1","doc2"], "encoding": "auto", "top_k": 5}``` error from client: "400 Bad Request: vector dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 512"
kevin_ml: that suggests the encoder being used by their client is returning 512-dim vectors (miniLM style) but the reranker/endpoint config expects 1536. two ways: change encoder to a 1536 model or configure reranker to accept 512. which reranker model is configured on your POC?
joe_customer: the POC guide said "use redwood/rew-embed-1536" — but our OSS encoder is defaulting to MiniLM for speed. can we keep MiniLM and do a transform?
emily_eng: you can project 512->1536 but that usually hurts quality. better options: (1) switch encoder to a 1536-compatible model, (2) update the Rerank route to accept 512 and use a compatible reranker variant, or (3) run an intermediate upsampler (ugly). For POC I'd recommend switching encoder to "semantic-embed-1536" on the client.
tariq_support: also saw the 429s in our logs — looks like bursts of parallel batches exceed the hosted API rate (we have small POC quota). we throttled at ~120 req/s and they popped >300 for a short window. we returned 429 with Retry-After header.
sara_sales: customer asked whether we can temporarily increase their POC rate/credits while they test — is that possible?
emily_eng: yes sales can ask ops to bump quota for a limited time. ping on headroom and we can flip rate limit config for their org id. but first let's fix dims mismatch so we don't waste headroom.
kevin_ml: to help, share a minimal repro. e.g.:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-large-v1","input":["hello world"]}'``` If that returns 512 we know the model mapping is wrong. If 1536, then the client encoder is the culprit.
joe_customer: running the curl now...
redwood-bot: deploy-hook: routing-config updated for org: acct-88 (no downtime)
joe_customer: curl returned 512. looks like our model id is being rewritten by our wrapper — we use an internal alias that points to miniLM in their config.
emily_eng: ok that explains dims. two threads: 1) change alias to semantic-1536 or call the explicit model id; 2) for rate surge, add client-side queueing/batching: reduce parallelism to <=8 and use max_batch_size:16. We'll provide recommended client config.
kevin_ml: sample client patch:```js
// batcher config
{
  maxConcurrentRequests: 8,
  maxBatchSize: 16,
  backoff: {strategy: "exponential", baseMs: 200}
}
```
sara_sales: i'll escalate quota bump in the billing portal and request a 2x headroom for 48h. sales note: customer also hit a security review question about "where embeddings are stored" — can someone from infra confirm retention?
tariq_support: infra/ops: embeddings are not persisted by default in hosted mode unless customer enables "cache/persist". we store ephemeral KV for prefix caching (TTL 1h) unless configured otherwise; we can share SOC2-compliant docs.
joe_customer: that helps. last ask: what about encoding mismatch causing rerank failures mid-batch (some vectors 512, some 1536) — we saw the reranker crash.
emily_eng: reranker expects homogeneous dims. if mixed dims land in same batch you get a hard error. best practice: enforce consistent encoder across the client or add a validation step before sending: check vector.length == model_dim. we can add a soft-fail hook that logs and drops mismatched items with a 200 + partial results for POC.
kevin_ml: opened a small PR with a defensive validator and a flag `allow_partial_batches` for client SDK. will drop into customer's repo if they want.
sara_sales: thanks all. next steps for us: 1) joe to switch alias to semantic-1536 or call explicit id (deadline today), 2) sara to request temporary quota bump, 3) kevin to send validator patch, 4) tariq to share retention + SOC2 note. i'll follow up with a quick summary and a support ticket link. :thumbsup:
joe_customer: switching alias now, will report back in ~20m. thanks!
kevin_ml: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/clients/pull/482 (contains config snippet and validate hook)
tariq_support: docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/embeddings-retention (SOC2 section included)
sara_sales: created support ticket #4521 for quota bump and attached logs. last_message_ts: 1876543287
